liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (2 reviews): Taper says the opening Jack Straw sounded heartfelt from the first notes on the tape; Opens after about 68 seconds of crowd noise and tuning; patient pace, Bobby not quite ready, others strong [13][17]
- **Box Of Rain** (2 reviews): Reviewer describes a crowd sing-along feel, with everyone happy the band is back on stage; Reviewer recalls a lasting feeling of joy and floating across the meadow near the end [17][20]
- **Stuck Inside Of Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again** (2 other sources): This song was patched in from a source supplied by digihoarders [1][4]
- **Loser** (2 reviews): Reviewer praises Jerry's singing and solo, and his feedback at the end; Reviewer lists Jack Straw, Box of Rain, Loser and Cassidy as first-set highlights [20][22]
- **Blow Away** (2 reviews): Reviewer says Brent sang a memorable line about lacking love; calls this the first Blow Away; Reviewer notes the first Blow Away was played at this show [12][19]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer at the show found Terrapin Station awesome, along with The Other One; This version of Terrapin Station lacks the issues found in the earlier source [2][12]
- **West L.A. Fadeaway** (1 review): Reviewer says the intro feels like Minglewood in approach, though less loose for dancing [17]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Bobby's performance on Cassidy [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-06-20.151410.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1988-06-20.123452.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 142 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1988-06-20.151614.UltraMatrix.sbd.1stGen.voss.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 146 min [4]
- **gd88-06-20.sennheiser.ladner.17269.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 137 min; rated 4.24/5 by 21 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says a tape from a taper years ago sounded much better than this audience recording; Reviewer calls the Alpine Valley audience recordings very good, especially the first night, with natural ambience; Reviewer rates it an A-quality audience recording and wonders whether a soundboard exists [12][15][16][18]

## Around the show

- Taper says the show felt like forced work, perhaps from the heat, and he left quickly afterward [13]
- Reviewer recalls possible radio frequency interference breaking in during space on one of these nights [16]
- Reviewer describes a dust bowl lot, with a bus full of flies and dust, selling soda and juice [18]
- Reviewer recalls 110-degree daytime heat on the sloping lawn [21]
- Reviewer calls the show the same as the night before: great show, okay recording [18]
- Reviewer, who saw about a dozen Alpine Valley shows, says this may be the best he has seen [21]
- Says second half of second set was the best part, unlike the awful equivalent stretch at the next show [22]
- First set is unchanged from the earlier source, shnid 119380 [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-06-20.151410.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  January 7, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M) > Cassette (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell XLII-S) [1]
- **gd1988-06-20.123452.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Set 1: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette (Sony D5/Dolby B)Set 2: SBD -> Cassette Master -> ? -> Cassette [2]. Also: Second set is a bit clearer than the earlier source; Joe B. Jones helped with pitch correction [2]
- **gd1988-06-20.151614.UltraMatrix.sbd.1stGen.voss.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Recorded by Jim Voss who copied Don Pearson's masters after the show; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  January 7, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M) > Cassette (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell XLII-S) [4]. Also: First-generation Voss recording, copied from Don Pearson's masters; 24-bit source converted to 16-bit at 44.1 [4]
- **gd88-06-20.sennheiser.ladner.17269.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Craig Camus; source: AUD(Senn 441's)>CM (Marantz PMD 430)>DAT>CDR>WAV>SHN. [6]
